items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: I’m taking down one of the tunes on this album which is “Spirit of the Moment” which is Joshua Redman’s album

ctx.x: hear often times standards and things they knew. So does your audience respond or behave differently than if they went to a club and someone was playing “All the Things You Are” and we hear, you know, a little applause after everybody’s solo. I’m imagining that your setting is somewhat different than that.

It can be. Yes. I would say, I mean I do a lot of varied work. My favorite kind of concert is really almost a chamber music concert you know, where people are really turning out to listen and there’s an atmosphere and there’s a sort of responsiveness – that kind of setting. And a lot of the time in that sort of setting I get audience members coming up to me at the end saying, “I was really moved” which makes me so happy because I think that’s such a gift to be able to give something to the world which is going to…

Do you feel it’s helpful to – I’ll use the word “explain” -- if you introduce one of your original compositions do you want to give the audience some backstory to it? Maybe where the title came from or just the intent? Or do you just let them explore that themselves?
